name: Glycogen Storage Disease with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glycogen Storage Disease with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with glycogen storage disease (e.g., PRKAG2, GAA)
Echocardiographic evidence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular wall thickness >15 mm
Muscle biopsy demonstrating excessive glycogen accumulation in cardiac or skeletal muscle tissue
Presence of exercise intolerance, arrhythmias, or conduction abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of genetic confirmation plus echocardiographic evidence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; muscle biopsy and clinical features supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for definitive diagnosis; differential diagnosis includes other causes of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Left ventricular hypertrophy with glycogen accumulation
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic hypertrophy due to glycogen storage
searchTerms: thickened heart muscle with glycogen buildup
enlarged left heart ventricle due to sugar storage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Conduction system abnormalities including Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems including WPW syndrome
abnormal heart conduction with extra pathway

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to cardiac dysfunction
searchTerms: poor exercise tolerance due to heart issues

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness related to glycogen accumulation
searchTerms: muscle fatigue related to sugar storage
weak muscles due to glycogen deposits

common.symptomName: Arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia
searchTerms: fast irregular heartbeats like AF or VT
passing out caused by heart rhythm problems

rare.symptomName: Heart failure symptoms including peripheral edema
searchTerms: heart failure with swelling in legs
symptoms of heart failure including leg swelling

rare.symptomName: Neurological manifestations such as peripheral neuropathy

laboratory: Elevated liver transaminases in some cases
imaging: Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial glycogen deposition and fibrosis
genetic: Mutations in GAA gene in Pompe disease variants
other: Muscle biopsy with periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) positive glycogen deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of glycogen accumulation on biopsy
Lack of systemic glycogen storage manifestations
Predominant skeletal muscle weakness with respiratory failure
Less prominent hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in late-onset forms

redFlags: Rapid progression of cardiac hypertrophy with arrhythmias
Severe exercise intolerance with muscle weakness
